label: lem:lpf_monotone_along_decomp
title: Least-prime-factor monotonicity along the decomposition
statement:
Let $m\ge 2$, and let $p$ be the least prime factor of $m$.
    Suppose $m=ap$.
    Then every prime divisor $q$ of $a$ satisfies $p\le q$.
    In particular, if $a\ge 2$, then $p \le \mathrm{lp}(a)$.
proof: If $q$ is a prime divisor of $a$, then by \ref{lem:divisor_lifts_to_product}, $q \mid ap = m$. Since $p$ is the least prime factor of $m$, we have $p \le q$.
